turns.learner: Hello! Can you give me an exercise on the past simple with -ed?
turns.tutor:
Quick reminder: regular verbs form the past simple with -ed, as in played or visited.
The more interesting part is spelling. A one-syllable verb ending in one vowel plus one consonant usually doubles that consonant (stop becomes stopped). A verb ending in a consonant plus y changes y to -ied (carry becomes carried). A verb ending in e just takes -d (smile becomes smiled).
Your task: write two sentences about last weekend. Use one regular verb that doubles its final consonant and one that changes y to -ied, both different from my examples. Then say in one line what makes each spelling change.
